NASB.1: So David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam; and when his brothers and all his father's household heard [of it], they went down there to him.
NASB.2: Everyone who was in distress, and everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was discontented gathered to him; and he became captain over them. Now there were about four hundred men with him.
NASB.3: And David went from there to Mizpah of Moab; and he said to the king of Moab, 'Please let my father and my mother come [and stay] with you until I know what God will do for me.'
NASB.4: Then he left them with the king of Moab; and they stayed with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.
NASB.5: The prophet Gad said to David, 'Do not stay in the stronghold; depart, and go into the land of Judah.' So David departed and went into the forest of Hereth.
NASB.6: Then Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree on the height with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.
NASB.7: Saul said to his servants who stood around him, 'Hear now, O Benjamites! Will the son of Jesse also give to all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make you all commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?
NASB.8: 'For all of you have conspired against me so that there is no one who discloses to me when my son makes [a covenant] with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you who is sorry for me or discloses to me that my son has stirred up my servant against me to lie in ambush, as [it is] this day.'
NASB.9: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing by the servants of Saul, said, 'I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
NASB.10: 'He inquired of the LORD for him, gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.'
NASB.11: Then the king sent someone to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father's household, the priests who were in Nob; and all of them came to the king.
NASB.12: Saul said, 'Listen now, son of Ahitub.' And he answered, 'Here I am, my lord.'
NASB.13: Saul then said to him, 'Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me, in that you have given him bread and a sword and have inquired of God for him, so that he would rise up against me by lying in ambush as [it is] this day?'
NASB.14: Then Ahimelech answered the king and said, 'And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, even the king's son-in-law, who is captain over your guard, and is honored in your house?
NASB.15: 'Did I [just] begin to inquire of God for him today? Far be it from me! Do not let the king impute anything to his servant [or] to any of the household of my father, for your servant knows nothing at all of this whole affair.'
NASB.16: But the king said, 'You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's household!'
NASB.17: And the king said to the guards who were attending him, 'Turn around and put the priests of the LORD to death, because their hand also is with David and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not reveal it to me.' But the servants of the king were not willing to put forth their hands to attack the priests of the LORD.
NASB.18: Then the king said to Doeg, 'You turn around and attack the priests.' And Doeg the Edomite turned around and attacked the priests, and he killed that day eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
NASB.19: And he struck Nob the city of the priests with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and infants; also oxen, donkeys, and sheep [he struck] with the edge of the sword.
NASB.20: But one son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.
NASB.21: Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
NASB.22: Then David said to Abiathar, 'I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I have brought about [the death] of every person in your father's household.
NASB.23: 'Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks my life seeks your life, for you are safe with me.'

NKJV.1: David therefore departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. So when his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, they went down there to him.
NKJV.2: And everyone who was in distress, everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was discontented gathered to him. So he became captain over them. And there were about four hundred men with him.
NKJV.3: Then David went from there to Mizpah of Moab; and he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother come here with you, till I know what God will do for me.”
NKJV.4: So he brought them before the king of Moab, and they dwelt with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.
NKJV.5: Now the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold; depart, and go to the land of Judah.” So David departed and went into the forest of Hereth.
NKJV.6: When Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered—now Saul was staying in Gibeah under a tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants standing about him—
NKJV.7: then Saul said to his servants who stood about him, “Hear now, you Benjamites! Will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands and captains of hundreds?
NKJV.8: All of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who reveals to me that my son has made a covenant with the son of Jesse; and there is not one of you who is sorry for me or reveals to me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day.”
NKJV.9: Then answered Doeg the Edomite, who was set over the servants of Saul, and said, “I saw the son of Jesse going to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
NKJV.10: And he inquired of the LORD for him, gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
NKJV.11: So the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests who were in Nob. And they all came to the king.
NKJV.12: And Saul said, “Hear now, son of Ahitub!” He answered, “Here I am, my lord.”
NKJV.13: Then Saul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day?”
NKJV.14: So Ahimelech answered the king and said, “And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, who is the king’s son-in-law, who goes at your bidding, and is honorable in your house?
NKJV.15: Did I then begin to inquire of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king impute anything to his servant, or to any in the house of my father. For your servant knew nothing of all this, little or much.”
NKJV.16: And the king said, “You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”
NKJV.17: Then the king said to the guards who stood about him, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled and did not tell it to me.” But the servants of the king would not lift their hands to strike the priests of the LORD.
NKJV.18: And the king said to Doeg, “You turn and kill the priests!” So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck the priests, and killed on that day eighty-five men who wore a linen ephod.
NKJV.19: Also Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and nursing infants, oxen and donkeys and sheep—with the edge of the sword.
NKJV.20: Now one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.
NKJV.21: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the LORD’s priests.
NKJV.22: So David said to Abiathar, “I knew that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I have caused the death of all the persons of your father’s house.
NKJV.23: Stay with me; do not fear. For he who seeks my life seeks your life, but with me you shall be safe.”

NLT.1: So David left Gath and escaped to the cave of Adullam. Soon his brothers and all his other relatives joined him there.
NLT.2: Then others began coming — men who were in trouble or in debt or who were just discontented — until David was the captain of about 400 men.
NLT.3: Later David went to Mizpeh in Moab, where he asked the king, “Please allow my father and mother to live here with you until I know what God is going to do for me.”
NLT.4: So David’s parents stayed in Moab with the king during the entire time David was living in his stronghold.
NLT.5: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Leave the stronghold and return to the land of Judah.” So David went to the forest of Hereth.
NLT.6: The news of his arrival in Judah soon reached Saul. At the time, the king was sitting beneath the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, holding his spear and surrounded by his officers.
NLT.7: “Listen here, you men of Benjamin!” Saul shouted to his officers when he heard the news. “Has that son of Jesse promised every one of you fields and vineyards? Has he promised to make you all generals and captains in his army?
NLT.8: Is that why you have conspired against me? For not one of you told me when my own son made a solemn pact with the son of Jesse. You’re not even sorry for me. Think of it! My own son — encouraging him to kill me, as he is trying to do this very day!”
NLT.9: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing there with Saul’s men, spoke up. “When I was at Nob,” he said, “I saw the son of Jesse talking to the priest, Ahimelech son of Ahitub.
NLT.10: Ahimelech consulted the LORD for him. Then he gave him food and the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
NLT.11: King Saul immediately sent for Ahimelech and all his family, who served as priests at Nob.
NLT.12: When they arrived, Saul shouted at him, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub!” “What is it, my king?” Ahimelech asked.
NLT.13: “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me?” Saul demanded. “Why did you give him food and a sword? Why have you consulted God for him? Why have you encouraged him to kill me, as he is trying to do this very day?”
NLT.14: “But sir,” Ahimelech replied, “is anyone among all your servants as faithful as David, your son-in-law? Why, he is the captain of your bodyguard and a highly honored member of your household!
NLT.15: This was certainly not the first time I had consulted God for him! May the king not accuse me and my family in this matter, for I knew nothing at all of any plot against you.”
NLT.16: “You will surely die, Ahimelech, along with your entire family!” the king shouted.
NLT.17: And he ordered his bodyguards, “Kill these priests of the LORD, for they are allies and conspirators with David! They knew he was running away from me, but they didn’t tell me!” But Saul’s men refused to kill the LORD’s priests.
NLT.18: Then the king said to Doeg, “You do it.” So Doeg the Edomite turned on them and killed them that day, eighty-five priests in all, still wearing their priestly garments.
NLT.19: Then he went to Nob, the town of the priests, and killed the priests’ families — men and women, children and babies — and all the cattle, donkeys, sheep, and goats.
NLT.20: Only Abiathar, one of the sons of Ahimelech, escaped and fled to David.
NLT.21: When he told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD,
NLT.22: David exclaimed, “I knew it! When I saw Doeg the Edomite there that day, I knew he was sure to tell Saul. Now I have caused the death of all your father’s family.
NLT.23: Stay here with me, and don’t be afraid. I will protect you with my own life, for the same person wants to kill us both.”

CSB17.1: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. <sup>ⓘ</sup> When David’s brothers and his father’s whole family heard, they went down and joined him there.
CSB17.2: In addition, every man who was desperate, in debt, or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.3: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I know what God will do for me.”
CSB17.4: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
CSB17.5: Then the prophet Gad <sup>ⓚ</sup> said to David, “Don’t stay in the stronghold. Leave and return to the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
CSB17.6: Saul heard that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree <sup>ⓛ</sup> at the high place. His spear was in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.
CSB17.7: Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin: Is Jesse’s son going to give all of you fields and vineyards? Do you think he’ll make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds? <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.8: That’s why all of you have conspired against me! Nobody tells me <sup>[1]</sup> when my own son makes a covenant with Jesse’s son. <sup>ⓝ</sup> None of you cares about me <sup>ⓐ</sup> or tells me <sup>[2]</sup> that my son has stirred up my own servant to wait in ambush for me, as is the case today.”
CSB17.9: Then Doeg the Edomite, <sup>ⓑ</sup> who was in charge of Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw Jesse’s son come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.10: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him <sup>ⓓ</sup> and gave him provisions. <sup>ⓔ</sup> He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.” <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.11: The king sent messengers to summon the priest Ahimelech son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests in Nob. All of them came to the king.
CSB17.12: Then Saul said, “Listen, son of Ahitub!” “I’m at your service, <sup>ⓖ</sup> my lord,” he said.
CSB17.13: Saul asked him, “Why did you and Jesse’s son conspire against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him, so he could rise up against me and wait in ambush, as is the case today.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.14: Ahimelech replied to the king: “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David? <sup>ⓘ</sup> He is the king’s son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard, and honored in your house.
CSB17.15: Was today the first time I inquired of God for him? <sup>ⓙ</sup> Of course not! Please don’t let the king make an accusation against your servant or any of my father’s family, for your servant didn’t have any idea <sup>[3]</sup> about all this.”
CSB17.16: But the king said, “You will die, Ahimelech — you and your father’s whole family!”
CSB17.17: Then the king ordered the guards standing by him, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD <sup>ⓚ</sup> because they sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they didn’t tell me.” <sup>[4]</sup> But the king’s servants would not lift a hand to execute the priests of the LORD.
CSB17.18: So the king said to Doeg, “Go and execute the priests!” So Doeg the Edomite went and executed the priests himself. On that day, he killed eighty-five men <sup>ⓛ</sup> who wore linen ephods. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.19: He also struck down Nob, the city of the priests, with the sword — both men and women, infants and nursing babies, oxen, donkeys, and sheep. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.20: However, one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and he fled to David. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.21: Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
CSB17.22: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite <sup>ⓒ</sup> was there that day and that he was sure to report to Saul. I myself am responsible for <sup>[5]</sup> the lives of everyone in your father’s family.
CSB17.23: Stay with me. Don’t be afraid, for the one who wants to take my life wants to take your life. <sup>ⓓ</sup> You will be safe with me.”

WEB.1: David therefore departed from there, and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, they went down there to him.
WEB.2: Everyone who was in distress, everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was discontented, gathered themselves to him; and he became captain over them. There were with him about four hundred men.
WEB.3: David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab, and he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and my mother come out with you, until I know what God will do for me.”
WEB.4: He brought them before the king of Moab; and they lived with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.
WEB.5: The prophet Gad said to David, “Don’t stay in the stronghold. Depart, and go into the land of Judah.” Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hereth.
WEB.6: Saul heard that David was discovered, with the men who were with him. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.
WEB.7: Saul said to his servants who stood around him, “Hear now, you Benjamites! Will the son of Jesse give everyone of you fields and vineyards? Will he make you all captains of thousands and captains of hundreds,
WEB.8: that all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who discloses to me when my son makes a treaty with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you who is sorry for me, or discloses to me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as it is today?”
WEB.9: Then Doeg the Edomite, who stood by the servants of Saul, answered and said, “I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
WEB.10: He inquired of Yahweh for him, gave him food, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
WEB.11: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests who were in Nob; and they all came to the king.
WEB.12: Saul said, “Hear now, you son of Ahitub.” He answered, “Here I am, my lord.”
WEB.13: Saul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread, and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as it is today?”
WEB.14: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, “Who among all your servants is so faithful as David, who is the king’s son-in-law, and is taken into your council, and is honorable in your house?
WEB.15: Have I today begun to inquire of God for him? Be it far from me! Don’t let the king impute anything to his servant, nor to all the house of my father; for your servant knows nothing of all this, less or more.”
WEB.16: The king said, “You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you, and all your father’s house.”
WEB.17: The king said to the guard who stood about him, “Turn, and kill the priests of Yahweh; because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he fled, and didn’t disclose it to me.” But the servants of the king wouldn’t put out their hand to fall on the priests of Yahweh.
WEB.18: The king said to Doeg, “Turn and attack the priests!” Doeg the Edomite turned, and he attacked the priests, and he killed on that day eighty-five people who wore a linen ephod.
WEB.19: He struck Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and nursing babies, and cattle and donkeys and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
WEB.20: One of the sons of Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
WEB.21: Abiathar told David that Saul had slain Yahweh’s priests.
WEB.22: David said to Abiathar, “I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I am responsible for the death of all the persons of your father’s house.
WEB.23: Stay with me. Don’t be afraid, for he who seeks my life seeks your life. For you will be safe with me.”

MSG.1: So David got away and escaped to the Cave of Adullam. When his brothers and others associated with his family heard where he was, they came down and joined him.
MSG.2: Not only that, but all who were down on their luck came around—losers and vagrants and misfits of all sorts. David became their leader. There were about four hundred in all.
MSG.3: Then David went to Mizpah in Moab. He petitioned the king of Moab, "Grant asylum to my father and mother until I find out what God has planned for me."
MSG.4: David left his parents in the care of the king of Moab. They stayed there all through the time David was hiding out.
MSG.5: The prophet Gad told David, "Don't go back to the cave. Go to Judah." David did what he told him. He went to the forest of Hereth.
MSG.6: Saul got word of the whereabouts of David and his men. He was sitting under the big oak on the hill at Gibeah at the time, spear in hand, holding court surrounded by his officials.
MSG.7: He said, "Listen here, you Benjaminites! Don't think for a minute that you have any future with the son of Jesse! Do you think he's going to hand over choice land, give you all influential jobs?
MSG.8: Think again. Here you are, conspiring against me, whispering behind my back—not one of you is man enough to tell me that my own son is making deals with the son of Jesse, not one of you who cares enough to tell me that my son has taken the side of this, this... outlaw!"
MSG.9: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul's officials, spoke up: "I saw the son of Jesse meet with Ahimelech son of Ahitub, in Nob.
MSG.10: I saw Ahimelech pray with him for God's guidance, give him food, and arm him with the sword of Goliath the Philistine."
MSG.11: Saul sent for the priest Ahimelech son of Ahitub, along with the whole family of priests at Nob. They all came to the king.
MSG.12:
Saul said, "You listen to me, son of Ahitub!"
"Certainly, master," he said.
MSG.13: "Why have you ganged up against me with the son of Jesse, giving him bread and a sword, even praying with him for God's guidance, setting him up as an outlaw, out to get me?"
MSG.14: Ahimelech answered the king, "There's not an official in your administration as true to you as David, your own son-in-law and captain of your bodyguard. None more honorable either.
MSG.15: Do you think that was the first time I prayed with him for God's guidance? Hardly! But don't accuse me of any wrongdoing, me or my family. I have no idea what you're trying to get at with this 'outlaw' talk."
MSG.16: The king said, "Death, Ahimelech! You're going to die—you and everyone in your family!"
MSG.17: The king ordered his henchmen, "Surround and kill the priests of God! They're hand in glove with David. They knew he was running away from me and didn't tell me." But the king's men wouldn't do it. They refused to lay a hand on the priests of God.
MSG.18: Then the king told Doeg, "You do it—massacre the priests!" Doeg the Edomite led the attack and slaughtered the priests, the eighty-five men who wore the sacred robes.
MSG.19: He then carried the massacre into Nob, the city of priests, killing man and woman, child and baby, ox, donkey, and sheep—the works.
MSG.20: Only one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped: Abiathar. He got away and joined up with David.
MSG.21: Abiathar reported to David that Saul had murdered the priests of God.
MSG.22: David said to Abiathar, "I knew it—that day I saw Doeg the Edomite there, I knew he'd tell Saul. I'm to blame for the death of everyone in your father's family.
MSG.23: Stay here with me. Don't be afraid. The one out to kill you is out to kill me, too. Stick with me. I'll protect you."
